what: Super Micro Computer builds servers. It assembles systems around Nvidia and other chips, specialising in rack-scale AI servers with liquid cooling, and ships them quickly after each new chip generation launches.
customers: Cloud providers, AI companies, enterprises and data centre operators building AI clusters.
money: AI and general purpose servers, racks and storage
moat: Speed to market with each new chip generation, built on a modular building-block design that lets it ship configurations before larger competitors finish qualifying theirs.
risks: Gross margin of 11% is thin because the chip cost dominates the system price
Accounting concerns led to a delayed annual report and an auditor resignation in 2024
It depends heavily on chip allocation from Nvidia
Revenue is concentrated in a few very large customers
opportunities: Revenue grew about 78% last year and about 76% a year over three years
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Cash of about $6.9 billion exceeds its debt
watch: Gross margin per system and whether revenue growth is matched by cash generation.
